payload.one_variable: VideoMAE position embedding resize: trilinear interpolation -> exact analytic regeneration. Backbone, learning rate, schedule, batch, seed and AMP dtype unchanged from V2-WS1.1b.
payload.purpose: VideoMAE stores a fixed analytic sinusoid position table whose every token has norm exactly sqrt(hidden/2). Resizing it from 16 to 32 frames by trilinear interpolation averages neighbouring rows out of phase and costs about 11 percent of that norm, measured at 0.888 for Base and 0.889 for Large. Evaluating the closed form at the required length is exact. This tests whether that degraded position signal was costing frame mAP.

payload.text: Hypothesis refuted, and the reasoning behind it was wrong. Regenerating the analytic table preserves the token norm exactly, but norm was never the objective. VideoMAE-Large was pretrained on 16-frame clips, so its encoder only ever saw flattened position indices 0 to 1567. Interpolation resamples that same learned index range onto 32 frames, which keeps every token inside the phase distribution the encoder was trained to read. Regeneration instead assigns indices 0 to 3135 on the original frequency schedule, so roughly half the tokens carry phase patterns the encoder has never seen. Interpolation is the more faithful operation for a pretrained encoder precisely because it is not analytically exact. The 11 percent norm loss is a symptom of resampling, not a defect to be fixed.

payload.rationale: Analytic regeneration costs 1.06 corrected frame mAP against interpolation (89.48 vs 90.54), missing the 91.04 gate by 1.56. Interpolation is retained as the default. The measured norm loss is real but is not a defect.

payload.one_variable: data.img_size 224 -> 288. Backbone, learning rate, schedule, batch, seed, AMP dtype and position-embedding mode unchanged from V2-WS1.1b.
payload.purpose: Input resolution 224 to 288. Resolution is the single best-evidenced recipe lever in the STAD literature: STAR measured 140x224 to 320x512 as +4.6 AVA mAP. The token grid goes from 14x14 to 18x18, so the position table is now resampled spatially as well as temporally, using interpolation, which V2-WS1.2 established is the right mode for a pretrained encoder.

payload.text: Resolution 288 costs 0.29 corrected frame mAP against 224 (90.25 final, 90.19 EMA, versus 90.54). Training loss was also worse at every epoch, 7.39 final against 7.05, so this is an optimisation effect rather than an evaluation artefact. The likely cause is that the VideoMAE position table must now be resampled spatially as well as temporally, from a 14x14 grid to 18x18. V2-WS1.2 already showed this encoder is sensitive to position resampling that moves tokens outside the pretraining distribution, and 288 compounds it. That is consistent with v1 also failing at 320, and means the published resolution evidence from STAR does not transfer here: STAR trains its own encoder at the target resolution rather than resampling a 224-pretrained table. Reaching higher resolution would need either a backbone pretrained at that size or a proper windowed-attention adaptation, not a config change.

payload.rationale: Resolution 288 is 0.29 below the 224 control and 0.79 below the 91.04 gate. Rejected as a cheap recipe lever; a real higher-resolution result would need a backbone adapted to the resolution rather than a resampled position table.

payload.one_variable: tube fusion rule: a fused tube keeps only the frames of its highest-scoring member (--tube-frames top) instead of every frame any member covers (union, the rule of V2HO-FLIPTTA and the exploratory ensemble); boxes are still score-weighted over the members that have the frame, scores averaged over all views.
payload.purpose: Flip TTA and the exploratory 3-model ensemble both lost ~2.3-2.5 video AP50 on tune while frame mAP rose. The union rule lengthens fused tubes, which lowers temporal overlap; keeping the top member's extent should remove that loss. Motivated by those results, so it is checked only on data they did not touch.
